ctx: 同事早上在電梯遇到你
line: Good morning! How are you today?
a: Not bad, thanks. You?
d: I'm thirty-two years old this year.
ex: 回應寒暄後反問對方最自然;其他選項文法錯或答非所問。

line: Are you ready to order?
a: Could we have a few more minutes, please?
d: Yes, I want order now, give me the menu again.
ex: 還沒決定時禮貌請對方多給幾分鐘;Go away 太無禮。

line: For here or to go?
a: To go, please.
d: I go to the office after this coffee.
ex: For here or to go 是問內用或外帶,答 To go 即外帶。

line: Do you have a reservation?
a: Yes, under the name Chen.
d: Yes, I reserved by Chen name.
ex: under the name ___ 是「用某某名字訂的」的慣用說法。

line: Do you have any liquids in your bag?
a: Just a small bottle of lotion.
d: No, I'm not thirsty right now.
The bag is mine, and I packed it all by myself this morning.
ex: liquids 指液體物品,不是問你渴不渴;直接說明帶了什麼。

line: Excuse me, is there a pharmacy near here?
a: Yes, there's one just around the corner.
d: You should see a doctor first, because a pharmacy can't help you.
ex: there's one around the corner = 轉角就有;「it has」是中式「有」。

line: Can I help you?
a: No thanks, I'm just looking.
d: You can't help me, because I already know what I want to buy.
Yes, I am a customer here.
ex: I'm just looking 是「隨便看看」標準說法;see see 是中式英文。

line: Thanks for the coffee!
a: You're welcome.
d: Don't thank me, it was very cheap.
ex: Never mind 是「算了、別在意」,不能拿來回應謝謝。

line: Sorry I'm late.
a: That's OK. We just started.
d: It doesn't matter, you are always late.
ex: 簡單接受道歉並說明狀況;指責對方總是遲到太失禮。

line: Hello, may I speak to Kevin?
a: Sure, just a moment, please.
d: Kevin is speaking now to you.
ex: 請對方稍等再轉接;Yes, you may speak 是字面誤解。

line: Nice to meet you.
a: Nice to meet you, too.
ex: 初次見面固定回 Nice to meet you, too。

line: That'll be 350 dollars.
a: Can I pay by card?
d: 350 dollars is too expensive, give me cheaper price.
ex: 店員已報價,接著問付款方式最自然;便利商店不議價,殺價很突兀。

line: Do you want to get lunch together?
a: Sure, where do you want to go?
d: Yes, I want get lunch together with you at the restaurant.
ex: 答應並問去哪裡;單說 No 太生硬,拒絕要給理由。

line: Where to?
a: Taipei Main Station, please.
ex: Where to? 是司機問目的地,直接說地點加 please。

line: How many nights will you be staying?
a: Three nights.
d: I stay very well, thank you.
ex: 問住幾晚,直接答數量即可。

line: Have a nice weekend!
a: Thanks, you too!
ex: You too 回祝對方;Same same 是中式說法。

ctx: 用餐快結束,服務生來問
line: How was everything?
a: It was delicious, thank you.
d: I have finished eat everything, and now I am very full.
ex: 問餐點如何,給評價並道謝。

line: What seems to be the problem?
a: I've had a sore throat since Monday.
d: Since Monday I have sore throat until now still.
ex: have had ... since 描述持續到現在的症狀。

ctx: 你坐在咖啡店,有人指著你旁邊空位
line: Is this seat taken?
a: No, go ahead.
ex: 問「有人坐嗎」,沒人坐要答 No;答 Yes 等於說有人。

line: Can you help me carry this box?
a: Sure, no problem.
d: I can, but I don't want to.
ex: 爽快答應;Of course not 是拒絕,語氣很衝。

line: Do you need a bag?
a: No, I'm fine, thanks.
d: I don't need it, you take it.
ex: I'm fine 在這裡是「不用了」的禮貌說法。

line: What do you usually do on weekends?
a: I usually go hiking or watch movies.
d: I went hiking last weekend with my cousins.
ex: 問平常習慣用現在簡單式回答;談上週末是答錯問題。

line: Window or aisle?
a: Aisle, please.
ex: 選擇題問句不能答 Yes,要選一個。

ctx: 幫同事接電話,對方說要找的人不在
line: Oh, he's not in? Can I leave a message?
a: Of course. Go ahead.
d: No, I don't have a message phone.
ex: 對方要留言,請他說即可;其他選項語意不通。

line: How was your weekend?
a: Great, I went to the beach.
d: It is great, I go to beach.
Next weekend I will rest at home.
ex: 談過去用過去式 went;談下週末是答非所問。

line: Excuse me, what time is it?
a: It's about half past three.
d: I have time, so I can talk with you if you want.
ex: half past three = 三點半。

line: Would you like something to drink?
a: Just water, please.
ex: Just ___, please 簡潔禮貌;Give me 太像命令。

line: Can you send me the file?
a: Sure, I'll send it now.
d: OK, I send you later now.
ex: I'll + 動詞表示當下決定要做;反問為什麼顯得不合作。

line: I passed my driving test!
a: Congratulations! That's great news.
d: I passed mine a long time ago, it's easy.
ex: Congratulations 要加 s;炫耀自己很早考過不得體。

line: Here's your key card. Your room is on the fifth floor.
a: Thank you. What time is breakfast?
d: OK, I go to five floor now and then I will sleep.
ex: 道謝後接著問早餐時間,自然順暢。

line: Would you like to try it on?
a: Yes. Where's the fitting room?
d: Yes, I like to try on it.
ex: fitting room 是試衣間;try it on 代名詞放中間。

line: Are you free tomorrow afternoon?
a: Yes, after two o'clock.
ex: 回答有空並給出時段,方便對方安排。

ctx: 朋友不小心打破你的杯子
line: I'm sorry, I broke your cup.
a: Don't worry about it.
d: You must pay me now, right now!
ex: Don't worry about it 是接受道歉的常用語。

line: Does this bus go to the airport?
a: No, you need the 1819.
ex: 直接回答並告訴對方該搭哪班車。

line: Could you speak more slowly, please?
a: Of course. Sorry about that.
ex: 同意並致歉;叫對方學英文非常失禮。

ctx: 朋友問你生日想要什麼
line: What would you like for your birthday?
a: Nothing special — just dinner together.
d: My birthday is in May, on the twentieth, just after my sister's.
ex: 回答想要什麼;說生日日期是答非所問。

line: We don't have this in a medium, sorry.
a: That's OK. Do you have it in a large?
d: OK, then I take small medium size, it's the same thing for me.
ex: in a large 指「L 號的」;Why not? 語氣不耐煩。

line: Do you mind if I open the window?
a: Not at all. Go ahead.
ex: Do you mind 問「介意嗎」,同意要答 Not at all;Yes 表示介意。

line: Can I see your passport, please?
a: Sure, here you are.
ex: 遞東西說 Here you are。

line: Hi, are we still meeting at 3?
a: Yes, see you in Room B.
d: We met at 3 yesterday, and the meeting was very long and boring.
ex: 確認仍照原定並補充地點。

line: Can you check this link? It doesn't open for me.
a: Sure, give me a sec.
d: It doesn't open for me too.
ex: give me a sec = 給我一下;否定句的「也」要用 either。

line: Running 10 mins late, sorry!
a: No worries, I'll grab a table.
d: OK, I am late too 10 mins, so we both arrive at same time.
ex: No worries 表示沒關係;grab a table 先佔位子。

line: Table for one?
a: No, two. My friend is coming.
d: Yes, it's for one person two.
ex: 直接更正人數並說明朋友稍後到。

line: Is everything OK with your room?
a: Yes, it's great, but the Wi-Fi is a bit slow.
d: My room is OK with me, with my room.
ex: 先肯定再委婉提出小問題,很自然。

line: Let's meet at 7.
a: Sounds good. See you then.
d: I meet you 7 clock at the station, don't be late again please.
ex: Sounds good 是固定說法,不說 sounds well。

line: Cash or card?
a: Card, please.
ex: 二選一問句要選一個,不能答 Yes。

line: Sorry, could you repeat that?
a: Sure. I said the meeting is moved to Thursday.
d: I already said it once. You should listen more carefully next time.
ex: 重述重點;I already said it 顯得不耐煩。

line: How do I get to the MRT station?
a: Go straight and turn left at the bank.
d: Go straight and left turn at bank and you arrive it.
The MRT is fast and clean.
ex: turn left at ___ 是指路基本句型。

line: Are you hungry?
a: A little. Let's eat something.
d: I was hungry yesterday, but today I am not so hungry like yesterday.
ex: hungry 是形容詞,要用 I'm hungry;A little 簡潔自然。

line: Are you allergic to anything?
a: Yes, I'm allergic to penicillin.
ex: allergic to + 物品;allergy 是名詞。

line: Thanks for your help today.
a: Anytime.
d: Yes, I helped you a lot today.
ex: Anytime = 隨時樂意幫忙;Never mind 用錯場合。

line: Sorry, we're closing in five minutes.
a: Oh, OK. I'll be quick.
d: Five minutes is OK, I stay one hour.
ex: 表示理解並會加快;質問為何打烊不禮貌。

line: Would you like some cake?
a: Yes, please. It looks great.
d: Yes, I would like some cakes please give me.
ex: I'm diet 是中式英文,應說 I'm on a diet。

ctx: 新同事自我介紹後問你
line: Where are you from?
a: I'm from Hsinchu, in Taiwan.
d: I'm going to Hsinchu next week to visit my family and friends.
ex: I'm from ___ 說明出身地。

line: Is this your first time in Japan?
a: No, it's my third visit.
ex: third visit 用序數;Yes 和 second time 互相矛盾。

line: Hey, how did the presentation go?
a: Pretty well, thanks. They liked the demo.
d: Yes, I go to presentation and I talk about our new product demo.
ex: How did ___ go? 問結果如何,用過去式回答並補一句細節。

line: Does anyone have any questions before we move on?
a: Just one — when's the deadline for phase two?
d: Move on, please, this part is really boring.
ex: Just one 帶出問題,簡潔;說會議無聊非常失禮。

line: Could you cover for me at the 2 p.m. call?
a: Sure. Anything I should know beforehand?
d: Cover what? You should do it yourself, it's your call, not mine.
ex: cover for 是代班;答應並問需要先知道什麼。

line: Can you have the report ready by Friday?
a: Friday might be tight, but I'll do my best.
d: Friday is impossible, ask someone else.
I will try my best to finish it until Friday.
Yes, the report was ready on Friday.
ex: tight = 時間很緊;期限要用 by,不用 until。

line: I'm afraid the salmon is sold out tonight.
a: Oh, that's a shame. What would you recommend instead?
d: Then I go to another restaurant, bye.
ex: I'm afraid 是「恐怕」委婉語,不是害怕;請對方推薦替代。

line: I'm sorry, but check-in isn't until 3 p.m.
a: No problem. Could I leave my luggage here until then?
d: But I want check in now, I am very tired, you must give me room.
ex: 接受規定並詢問寄放行李,實用又禮貌。

line: We're having a barbecue on Saturday. Want to come?
a: I'd love to, but I'm visiting my parents. Next time?
d: Yes, but I can't come because I have to visit my parents that day.
ex: 婉拒公式:I'd love to, but + 理由 + 提議下次。

line: I'm not sure I follow. Could you explain that again?
a: Sure — basically, we're switching suppliers to cut costs.
d: Yes, I could explain that again.
ex: follow 在此是「聽懂」;用 basically 換句話簡述。

line: Could I have your account number, please?
d: Yes, you could have my account.
ex: 直接提供號碼;You could have 是字面誤解。

line: Your flight has been delayed by two hours.
a: Oh no. Will I still make my connection in Tokyo?
d: That's your problem, not mine. I need to be in Tokyo on time today.
ex: make my connection = 趕得上轉機,是最實際的追問。

line: Would you like to keep the receipt?
a: Yes, please — just in case.
d: Keep it to you, I don't need any paper, I have my phone.
ex: just in case = 以防萬一;No 和 I'll keep it 矛盾。

line: I think we should postpone the launch.
a: I see your point, but the client is expecting it next week.
d: Postpone is good idea, yes, no.
I think so too, so we should launch now.
ex: I see your point, but… 是委婉表達不同意的常用句。

line: Sorry to interrupt, but we're running out of time.
a: Right, let's wrap up the last item quickly.
d: Sorry, I am interrupting too, but I think we still have a lot of time.
ex: wrap up = 收尾;接受提醒並加快進度。

line: Great job on the client meeting today.
a: Thanks! The team prepared really well.
d: Yes, I know I am great. I always do the best job in this team.
ex: 接受稱讚並歸功團隊;過度否定或自誇都不自然。

line: Sorry for the wait. Here's your pasta.
a: Thanks. Could we also get some more bread?
d: It's OK, never mind, I waited very long.
ex: 大方接受並提出新需求;直說太慢不禮貌。

line: Is everything all right here?
a: Actually, I ordered the chicken, not the beef.
d: Everything is not right here, you are terrible, bring the manager now.
Yes, but this is wrong food.
ex: Actually 開頭委婉指出問題,清楚又不衝。

line: How long have you had this cough?
a: About a week now.
d: I have it a week ago.
ex: How long 問期間,答 About a week;since 後面要接時間點。

line: Take this twice a day after meals.
a: Got it. Should I avoid alcohol?
d: OK, two times one day eat, after breakfast and dinner, I remember.
ex: Got it 表示了解,再問相關注意事項。

line: I'm thinking of quitting my job.
a: Really? What happened?
d: Good, you should quit. That company is terrible anyway.
ex: 先關心原因;直接叫人辭職太草率。

line: Do you know where the projector remote is?
a: I think Amy had it in the meeting room.
d: Yes, it's a remote. It's for controlling the projector from far.
ex: Do you know where 要回答地點,單說 I know 不夠。

line: Would you mind switching seats so I can sit with my son?
a: Not at all. Which seat is yours?
d: I don't mind to switch you, but my seat is better than your seat.
ex: Would you mind 同意要說 Not at all。

line: Want to grab a coffee after this?
a: I'd love to, but I have another call. Rain check?
d: I don't drink coffee with you.
Grab is not a polite word. You should say 'Would you like to have'.
Yes, after this I grab you.
ex: rain check = 改天再約,婉拒常用。

line: Could you send over the updated quote by end of day?
a: Will do — you'll have it by 5 p.m.
d: Okay, I will send you quote end day.
Why did you not ask earlier?
ex: Will do 是「好的,會處理」;再給明確時間。

line: Quick question — is the server down for you too?
a: Yeah, same here. IT is on it.
d: The server is down for me too?
ex: same here = 我也是;on it = 正在處理。

line: I've attached the draft. Let me know what you think.
a: Thanks — I'll take a look and get back to you this afternoon.
d: Thanks, I have attached it too.
OK, I'll let you know what you think.
ex: get back to you = 再回覆你;最後一句人稱錯亂。

line: Hi, I'm calling about the job ad on your website.
a: Sure, which position are you interested in?
d: Why are you calling? You can just send email to our HR department.
ex: 確認對方想應徵哪個職位;Why are you calling 不禮貌且多餘。

ctx: 主管想改一對一面談時間
line: Can we move our one-on-one to Thursday?
a: Thursday works. Same time?
ex: ___ works 表示可以;再確認時間。

line: That one's on sale — 30% off.
a: Great. Does that include the jacket too?
d: Can you give me 50% off instead? Or I'm leaving this shop now.
ex: 追問折扣範圍很自然;威脅要走太衝。

line: Do you have the receipt?
a: I'm afraid I lost it. Can I still exchange it?
d: I have no receipt, but I have the item for you here in my bag.
ex: I'm afraid 委婉說壞消息,再問是否仍能換。

line: You look tired.
a: Yeah, I didn't sleep well last night.
d: You look tired too. Maybe we both need to go home early today.
ex: 說明原因自然;You look tired 不是稱讚,不用道謝。

line: I'm so sorry — I forgot to send you the minutes.
a: No worries. Could you send them today?
d: It doesn't matter, I don't care about minutes.
ex: minutes 指會議紀錄;接受道歉並提出期望。

line: Would you like a wake-up call?
a: Yes, at 6:30, please.
d: Yes, I would like to call.
I wake up at 6:30 every day.
ex: wake-up call 是叫醒服務,回答要幾點。

line: Did you pack your bag yourself?
a: Yes, I did.
d: Yes, I packed it by myself bag.
ex: 安檢固定問題,簡答 Yes, I did。

line: What do you think of the new office?
a: I like it — it's much brighter than the old one.
d: It's more bright than old one, and the chairs are more comfortable.
ex: bright 比較級是 brighter;給意見加理由。

line: We'd like to see a demo before we decide.
a: Of course. How about next Tuesday?
d: You should decide first, and then we can show you the demo later.
ex: 同意並主動提時間,推進流程。

line: I can't make it tonight, something came up.
a: That's OK. Hope everything's fine.
d: Why? What came up? Tell me.
ex: something came up 是委婉說有事;追問細節太冒昧。

line: Is it OK if I leave a bit early today? My kid is sick.
a: Of course. I hope she feels better soon.
d: OK, but who will do your work then?
ex: 同意並表達關心;質疑工作誰做顯得冷漠。

line: Is it within walking distance?
a: Yes, it's about ten minutes on foot.
d: Yes, you can walk distance, it is not so far from here to there.
ex: within walking distance = 走路可到;on foot = 步行。

line: What time would you like the table?
a: Around seven, if possible.
d: The table at seven o'clock would like.
ex: 問時間就答時間;Seven people 是答人數。

line: I need you to lead the project kickoff.
a: Sure. Who else will be in the meeting?
d: Why me? I think someone else in the team can do it better.
ex: kickoff 是專案啟動會議;接下並問細節。

line: Did you get my email?
a: I did, but I haven't had a chance to read it yet.
d: I got it, but not read yet it.
What email? I never read emails.
ex: haven't had a chance to = 還沒空去做。

line: Let's go around the table and introduce ourselves.
a: Hi everyone, I'm Jason from the data team.
d: I'm Jason, and you? Please introduce yourself to me also.
ex: 名字加所屬團隊是職場自我介紹基本款。

line: I'm sorry, this card was declined.
a: Oh, that's strange. Let me try another one.
d: Your machine is broken, I think. My card always works everywhere.
ex: declined = 刷卡被拒;冷靜換卡,不怪店家。

ctx: 朋友來家裡吃飯後道謝
line: Thanks for having us over. Dinner was amazing.
a: I'm glad you enjoyed it. Come again soon!
d: You're welcome to have us over. We will come to your house again.
ex: have someone over = 請人到家裡;回應感謝並邀再來。

ctx: 同事在講電話,你太大聲
line: Could you keep it down a little? I'm on a call.
a: Oh, sorry! I didn't realise.
ex: keep it down = 小聲點;立即致歉。

line: I'd like you to come back in two weeks.
a: Sure. Should I book that at the front desk?
d: Two weeks later I come back.
ex: 答應並詢問如何預約回診。

line: What's the Wi-Fi password?
a: It's on the whiteboard by the door.
d: I don't know where is it, maybe you can ask somebody else.
ex: 告訴對方在哪裡找;間接問句語序是 where it is。

line: Please confirm your attendance at the training on May 3.
a: Confirmed — I'll be there. Thanks.
ex: 簡短確認出席即可。

line: Are you coming to Amy's party?
a: Yes! What should I bring?
d: I came to Amy's party last year, it was really fun and crowded.
ex: 答應並問要帶什麼,很自然。

line: Can you jump on a quick call?
a: Sure, give me two minutes.
d: No, I'm too busy now, bye.
ex: jump on a call = 馬上通個電話。

line: I disagree. I think the old design was better.
a: Fair enough. What did you like about it?
d: I disagree your disagree, because the new design is more modern.
ex: Fair enough 先接住意見,再請對方說明。

line: Good news — your room has been upgraded to a suite.
a: Wow, thank you! That's very kind.
d: I don't want, give me small room.
Thank you for your upgrading me, I am very appreciate it.
ex: 開心道謝即可。

line: Can I get a name for the order?
a: Sure, it's Ken.
ex: 問名字就給名字;You can get 是字面誤解。

line: Would you be able to review my code this afternoon?
a: I can do it after lunch. Send me the PR link.
d: This afternoon is busy for me to review, maybe you ask other people.
ex: 答應並說時間、要連結,溝通清楚。

line: Do you mind if I take the highway? It's faster.
a: Not at all, go ahead.
ex: Do you mind 同意答 Not at all;I don't care 聽起來冷淡。

line: I think you have the wrong number.
a: Oh, I'm sorry to bother you.
d: Then who are you? I want to talk to Mr. Chen, please give him.
ex: 打錯電話就道歉掛斷。

line: How long have you worked here?
a: Almost three years now.
d: I worked here three years ago.
ex: How long 問期間,用 ___ years now 回答。

line: Do you want to split the bill?
a: Sure, let's go halves.
ex: go halves = 平分付款。

line: Could you give me a quick update on the project?
a: Sure — we're on track, but testing is a bit behind.
d: Why do you always ask me? I already sent you an update last month.
ex: on track = 進度正常;補充落後項目。

line: Anything to declare?
a: No, nothing.
d: Declare what? I don't understand you.
ex: declare 指申報物品,沒有就答 No, nothing。

line: Would you like to see the dessert menu?
a: We're fine, thanks. Just the check, please.
d: No, I'd like to see. Bring me the dessert menu and the check also.
ex: the check = 帳單;婉拒甜點直接買單。

line: It's my last day today.
a: Oh, really? We'll miss you. Keep in touch!
d: Congratulations, finally! You must be very happy to leave us.
ex: 表達不捨並保持聯絡;Finally 像是很高興他走。

line: Your package was delivered to my place by mistake.
a: Oh, thank you so much for letting me know!
d: Why did you take my package? You should give it to the guard.
ex: 感謝對方告知;質問很失禮。

line: Is this a gift? We can wrap it for you.
a: That would be great, thanks.
ex: That would be great 接受提議。

line: Are you using this machine?
a: Almost done — just one more set.
d: I use it every day at this time, so you can come back tomorrow.
ex: 告訴對方快好了,讓他能等。

line: Sorry, did I catch you at a bad time?
a: Actually, I'm about to go into a meeting. Can I call you back?
d: No, you didn't catch me. I am free, but I'm going into a meeting now.
ex: catch you at a bad time = 打擾到你;說明並約回電。

line: The plumber can come on Wednesday morning.
a: Perfect. I'll make sure someone's home.
d: Morning is no good, come at eleven p.m.
ex: 確認並安排有人在家。

line: I got the job!
a: That's fantastic! When do you start?
d: Congratulation for you! I knew you can get it because you are smart.
ex: 恭喜並問何時開始;不相信聽起來很傷人。

line: Can I borrow your charger for a minute?
a: Sure, here you go.
ex: borrow 借入、lend 借出;here you go 遞東西。

line: How would you like your steak?
a: Medium, please.
ex: 問熟度,答 rare/medium/well-done 之一。

line: Unfortunately, we need to reschedule Thursday's meeting.
a: No problem. Would Friday morning work for you?
d: OK, reschedule is fine for Thursday, see you on Thursday then.
ex: 接受並主動提新時間。

line: FYI, the deadline moved to next Monday.
a: Thanks for the heads-up!
d: Why didn't you tell me earlier?
ex: heads-up = 事先提醒;FYI = 供你參考。

line: Could you introduce me to someone on the legal team?
a: Sure — I'll cc you on an email to Grace.
d: You can find them by yourself on the company website, it's easy.
ex: 寫信給對方並副本(cc)給他,是常見引薦方式。

line: Just a reminder that rent is due on the 5th.
a: Thanks, I'll transfer it tomorrow.
ex: due = 到期;說明何時轉帳。

line: Have you met our new manager yet?
a: Not yet. What's she like?
d: I haven't meet her, but I heard she is very strict person.
ex: What's she like? 問人的個性;haven't 後接 met。

line: We can deliver it on Monday or Wednesday.
a: Wednesday would be better for me.
ex: better 本身已是比較級,不加 more。

line: I'm really nervous about my interview tomorrow.
a: You'll be fine. You've prepared a lot.
d: Why nervous? It's just an interview. I did many interviews before.
ex: 給予鼓勵;輕描淡寫對方的緊張顯得不體貼。

line: Let's touch base next week.
a: Sounds good. I'll set up a time.
ex: touch base = 簡短聯繫、對一下進度。

line: Do you have a minute?
a: Sure, what's up?
ex: Do you have a minute 是問方便聊嗎,不是真的一分鐘。

line: You need exact change.
a: Oh, can I use my transit card instead?
d: I have no exactly money, can you change for me one hundred dollars?
ex: exact change = 剛好的零錢,詢問能否用卡。

line: Is there anything I can do to help?
a: Actually, yes — could you check these numbers for me?
d: No, you can't help me, you're too slow.
ex: 接受幫忙並具體說要做什麼。

line: Have you been taking the medicine regularly?
a: Mostly, but I missed a couple of doses.
d: I take medicine regular, every day two times, but sometimes I forget.
ex: 誠實說明,missed doses = 漏吃幾次。

line: Sorry, I can't hear you — you're breaking up.
a: Let me call you back in a sec.
d: I'm not breaking up with you!
ex: breaking up 在電話中指斷訊,不是分手。

line: Sorry, could you remind me of your name?
a: Sure, it's Wei. We met at the training.
d: You forgot me? We met at the training only two weeks ago!
ex: 大方再說一次並提示在哪見過。

line: Would you like help with your bags?
a: That's OK, I can manage. Thanks.
ex: I can manage = 我自己來;婉拒要加謝謝。

line: Can everyone see my screen?
a: Yes, it's showing fine.
ex: 確認畫面有出來。

line: We apologise for the delay in your shipment.
a: Thanks for letting me know. Do you have a new delivery date?
d: Delay is your fault. If it happens again, I'll never order from you.
ex: 感謝告知並追問新日期。

line: Are you going to the team dinner on Friday?
a: I'm not sure yet. I'll let you know tomorrow.
d: I went to the team dinner last Friday, and the food was really good.
ex: 未定時說明何時回覆;Maybe yes maybe no 是中式。

line: I think we should cut the marketing budget by half.
a: That's an interesting idea, but I'm worried it might hurt our Q3 numbers.
d: I am agree with you partly not, because Q3 numbers are very important for us.
ex: 先肯定再提出顧慮,是外交式反對的典型句型。

line: Your price is about 15% higher than your competitor's.
a: I understand. Our price includes on-site support, though. Could we talk about volume?
d: Our price is higher because it's higher.
15% is not so much, just accept it.
ex: 說明價值並轉向數量折扣,保住談判空間。

line: I'd like you to take on the Singapore account as well.
a: I'd be happy to, but I'd need to hand off some of my current work. Can we discuss priorities?
ex: 答應但提出條件、討論優先順序,專業不吃虧。

line: Front desk, how can I help you?
a: Hi, I'm afraid the air conditioning in my room isn't working.
d: Your air conditioner in my room is broken, send someone to fix it now!
ex: I'm afraid 讓投訴聽起來客氣;命令式太兇。

ctx: 同事請你幫忙看投影片
line: Do you think you could take a look at my slides before tomorrow?
a: Happy to. I've got some time after four, if that works.
d: Yes, I think I could, but I'm not sure if I will have time or not.
ex: Happy to 爽快答應並給時段;Yes, I think I could 沒給下文。

ctx: 主管質問問題為何沒早點回報
line: Why wasn't this flagged earlier?
a: That's fair. I noticed it on Tuesday but underestimated the impact.
d: Because nobody asked me about it, so I thought it was not my job.
ex: 承認判斷失誤比推卸責任專業;flag = 提出警示。

line: We need the delivery two weeks earlier.
a: Let me check with production. Would a partial shipment help in the meantime?
d: You should have told us that before.
ex: 不直接拒絕,先查再提替代方案(分批出貨)。

line: What would you say is your biggest weakness?
a: I tend to take on too much myself, so I've been working on delegating earlier.
ex: 誠實說缺點並說明如何改善,是面試標準答法。

line: I'm swamped — is there any chance we could push back the review?
a: Sure, how about Thursday instead?
d: Swamped is busy? I don't understand swamped.
ex: swamped = 忙翻;push back = 延後。

line: I'm so sorry, the kitchen made a mistake with your order.
a: These things happen. How long will the new one take?
d: It's OK, mistakes are normal for you, I know this kitchen is always slow.
ex: These things happen 表示體諒,再問等待時間。

line: Would you mind keeping the music down after ten? My baby's sleeping.
a: Oh, I'm sorry — I had no idea. I'll keep it down.
d: It's my apartment, so I can listen to music any time I want.
ex: 致歉並配合;強調是自己家會引起衝突。

line: So are we all agreed on the timeline?
a: Mostly, but I'd like to revisit the testing phase — it looks tight.
d: Yes, we all are agreed totally.
ex: Mostly, but… 部分同意並提出要再討論的點。

line: We were disappointed with the quality of the last batch.
a: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you send photos of the issue so we can investigate?
ex: 先致歉再要具體資料,展現處理誠意。

line: I won't be able to make the deadline. Can we talk?
a: Thanks for flagging it early. I'm free at 2 — let's figure out a plan.
d: Why not? You had two weeks.
ex: 肯定對方提早告知,再約時間解決。

line: Hey, did you get a chance to look at my PR?
a: Not yet, sorry — it's next on my list.
d: I looked at your PR maybe.
Stop asking me about it, I'm busy.
ex: next on my list = 下一個就處理;不耐煩回應傷關係。

line: That's our final offer.
a: I appreciate that. Let me take it back to my team and get back to you tomorrow.
d: OK, I accept final, but give me more.
Fine, then we're done here, goodbye.
ex: 不當場決定,帶回討論,保留空間。

line: Your blood pressure is a little high.
a: Is that something I should be worried about?
d: A little high is OK for me, because my father also has high blood pressure.
ex: 詢問是否需擔心,是自然的追問。

line: Did you hear they're restructuring the department?
a: I've heard rumours, but nothing official yet.
d: They are restructuring me and my team, I'm very worried about my job.
ex: rumours = 傳聞;謹慎回應不散播。

ctx: 你是客服,客戶來電抱怨
line: I've been on hold for twenty minutes!
a: I'm really sorry about the wait. Let me sort this out for you now.
d: Sorry, I was having my lunch. Everybody needs to eat lunch, right?
ex: 先道歉再承諾處理;sort out = 解決。

line: I need this by tomorrow morning.
a: I can get you a first draft by then, but the full analysis will take until Thursday.
d: I'll try, but no promise, maybe.
ex: 給出可行的部分交付並說明完整時程。

ctx: 同事對你的方案有疑慮
line: I really don't think this approach will work.
a: What makes you say that?
d: OK, I don't think too, so it won't work.
ex: 開放提問了解疑慮,不急著辯護。

line: Do you fancy going to that new Thai place?
a: I'd be up for that. Is Saturday any good?
d: Fancy is expensive? I don't want to go to a fancy restaurant.
ex: fancy = 想要(英式);be up for = 有興趣。

line: I'm afraid this flight is overbooked. Would you be willing to take a later flight?
a: That depends. What kind of compensation are you offering?
d: Yes, I'm willing to be late flight, but you must give me business class.
ex: 超賣時先問補償再決定,合理且禮貌。

ctx: 會議中有人請你說清楚
line: Could you elaborate on that point?
a: Sure. What I mean is that the costs will shift to the customer, not disappear.
ex: elaborate = 詳細說明;What I mean is 換句話說。

line: How do you feel about relocating to the Kaohsiung office?
a: It's an interesting opportunity. Could I have a few days to talk it over with my family?
d: Kaohsiung is too hot for me and my family, so absolutely no way.
ex: 重大決定先爭取考慮時間;I feel good 答非所問。

line: Would you be open to co-presenting at the conference?
a: Definitely — I'd enjoy that. When's the submission deadline?
ex: be open to = 願意考慮;答應並問期限。

line: I'm going to have to raise the rent next year.
a: I see. Could you tell me by how much? I'd like to plan ahead.
d: You're greedy. The apartment is old and the rent is already too high.
ex: 冷靜詢問漲幅以便規劃。

line: We'd like to invite you for a second interview.
a: Thank you — I'd be delighted. I'm available any time Wednesday or Thursday.
d: Why not just hire me directly?
ex: 道謝並主動提供可行時段。

line: This item is non-refundable, but we can offer store credit.
a: I see. In that case, store credit is fine.
d: Store credit is what kind of card? I only want my money back in cash.
ex: store credit = 店內抵用金;OK, refund me 與對方說法矛盾。

line: Sorry, I think you're on mute.
a: Oops — can you hear me now?
ex: 解除靜音後確認對方聽得到。

line: Your proposal is a bit too long. Could you tighten it up?
a: Sure. Would a one-page summary with an appendix work?
d: It's long because it's important. I can't remove anything from it.
ex: tighten up = 精簡;提出具體改法。

line: I'm really sorry I snapped at you yesterday.
a: It's OK. I know you've been under a lot of pressure.
d: Snap is OK, I don't know what snap means but no problem for me.
ex: snap at = 對人發脾氣;表示理解對方壓力。

line: Is there any flexibility on the payment terms?
a: We could consider 60 days instead of 30 for orders above 500 units.
ex: 有條件讓步是談判常見做法。

line: Can I run something by you?
a: Of course, go ahead.
d: Run by me fast, because I have only one minute for you today.
ex: run something by someone = 請人聽聽看意見。

line: Can you loop in Daniel on this thread?
a: Done — just added him.
ex: loop in = 拉人進來討論。

line: I'd like to propose that we meet weekly instead of monthly.
a: I can see the benefit, though maybe every two weeks would be a good compromise?
d: Yes, I'd like to propose too.
ex: 肯定好處再提折衷方案(compromise)。

line: Unfortunately, your warranty expired last month.
a: That's a pity. Is there a paid repair option?
d: Warranty is your fault, you should tell me before it expired.
ex: 接受事實並詢問付費維修。

line: I've got a lot on my plate this week.
a: Want me to take the vendor calls off your hands?
d: Eat slower, then your plate will be empty soon.
So what? Everybody is busy this week, not only you.
ex: a lot on my plate = 事情很多;off your hands = 替你分擔。

line: I'd recommend some blood tests to rule out anything serious.
a: Sure. Do I need to fast beforehand?
d: Rule out is what? I don't understand, I think I'm not serious sick.
ex: rule out = 排除;fast 在此為空腹禁食。

line: Can you summarise the key takeaways from yesterday's workshop?
a: Sure — I'll send a short summary by noon.
d: Key takeaways: many, many. I can't remember all of them, sorry.
ex: takeaways = 重點收穫,不是外帶食物。

line: We're thinking of pivoting to a subscription model.
a: Interesting. Have we tested whether customers would pay monthly?
d: Subscription is good, everyone does it, just do it.
ex: pivot = 轉型;提出驗證問題是建設性回應。

line: We have no record of your booking, I'm afraid.
a: That's odd — I have a confirmation email. Could you check under my company name?
d: You lost it, it's your fault!
ex: 冷靜提供證據並請對方換方式查。

line: No offence, but your code is hard to read.
a: None taken. Any suggestions on what to change first?
d: Your code is harder to read than mine, so you shouldn't say that.
ex: None taken 是 No offence 的標準回應。

line: Do you know if the water will be off tomorrow?
a: I think it's just from 9 to noon — there's a notice in the lobby.
d: Ask the guard, not me. I'm not the building manager, you know.
ex: 提供資訊與來源;叫對方去問別人不友善。

line: Could you hold the line for a moment?
a: Sure, no problem.
d: No, I'm in a hurry, quickly, quickly.
ex: hold the line = 電話別掛,稍等。

line: I've decided to give the project to Anna.
a: I understand. Could I ask what I could do differently next time?
d: Anna is not good enough for it. I have more experience than her.
ex: 接受決定並請教改進,展現成熟。

line: Would you like to come to my wedding in Kyoto? I know it's far.
a: I'd be honoured. Let me check flights and confirm by the end of the month.
ex: 表達榮幸並給確認時間。

line: Just following up on my email from last week.
a: Apologies for the slow reply — I'll have an answer for you by tomorrow.
d: I was busy, don't push me.
ex: 致歉並承諾回覆時間。

line: Can we park that for now and come back to it?
a: Sure, let's add it to next week's agenda.
d: No, we discuss it now, because if we park it, everyone will forget.
ex: park = 先擱置;放入下次議程。

line: We can't do a refund without the original packaging.
a: I understand. Would it be possible to speak to a manager?
d: That's a stupid policy. No other shop asks for the original packaging.
ex: 有禮地要求找主管,而非攻擊政策。

line: I owe you one for covering my shift.
a: Don't mention it. You'd do the same for me.
d: Yes, you owe me one hundred dollars. Pay me back tomorrow, OK?
ex: I owe you one = 欠你一次;Don't mention it 別客氣。

line: Ugh, my flight got cancelled.
a: Oh no! Have they rebooked you?
d: You should buy a better airline.
ex: 表達同情並問後續;rebook = 改訂。

line: We're considering other vendors.
a: I understand. Is there anything specific we could improve to keep your business?
ex: 詢問改善點以留住客戶。

line: Can you walk me through the numbers?
a: Sure. Let's start with revenue.
d: The numbers are on page 3, read it.
ex: walk someone through = 帶人逐步說明。

line: I'm thinking of applying for the team lead role. Thoughts?
a: Go for it — you'd be great. Want me to look over your application?
d: Team lead is hard, forget it.
ex: Go for it = 放手去做;主動提供協助。

line: Frankly, I'm not convinced the numbers add up.
a: That's a fair challenge. Let me walk you through the assumptions.
d: You don't understand finance, so maybe you should ask the accounting team.
Frankly, me neither, but let's go ahead anyway.
ex: add up = 說得通;接受質疑並解釋假設。

line: Between you and me, I think the merger's going to fall through.
a: Really? What makes you think so?
d: Between you and me is a secret.
Interesting, I'll tell everyone in the team so they can be ready.
ex: fall through = 告吹;between you and me = 私下說。

line: I'll level with you — the budget's been slashed.
a: I appreciate you being upfront. Which projects are most affected?
d: Then I quit. I can't work on a project without enough money.
ex: level with = 坦白;upfront = 直接坦率。

line: We'd like to explore a longer-term partnership, provided the pilot goes well.
a: That sounds promising. Shall we agree upfront on what 'going well' looks like?
d: The pilot will definitely be perfect, sign now.
ex: provided = 前提是;先定義成功標準很專業。

line: I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but the client pulled out.
a: Ah, that's a blow. Did they give a reason?
d: Why do you always bring bad news? Can't you tell me something good?
ex: pull out = 退出;a blow = 打擊。

line: We're not in a position to commit to those volumes at this stage.
a: Understood. Would a smaller initial commitment with an option to scale work for you?
d: Then why are we even talking?
ex: 提出較小起始量加擴充選項,讓談判續行。

line: Let's not reinvent the wheel here.
a: Agreed — we can adapt last year's framework.
d: I don't reinvent anything, I only use what the company gives me.
ex: reinvent the wheel = 重新發明輪子、白費功夫。

line: With all due respect, that's not what the data shows.
a: Fair point — I may have oversimplified. Let me pull up the figures.
d: The data shows what I said. Maybe you are reading the wrong chart.
ex: With all due respect 是禮貌的反對;以數據回應。

line: I'm afraid we'll have to put the project on hold pending budget approval.
a: Understood. Please keep us posted, and let us know if we can prepare anything in the meantime.
ex: pending = 等待…期間;keep us posted = 隨時告知。

line: He's a bit of a loose cannon, isn't he?
a: He can be unpredictable, but his ideas are often good.
d: I'll tell him you said that, because I think he should know.
ex: loose cannon = 難以預測的人;平衡回應不落井下石。

line: I'm going to play devil's advocate for a second.
a: Go ahead — it's useful to stress-test the plan.
d: Don't be the devil, please. We need positive people in this team.
ex: play devil's advocate = 故意唱反調來檢驗想法。

line: That ship has sailed, I'm afraid.
a: Fair enough. Let's focus on what we can still influence.
d: Let's sail it again — we can still try to catch the ship tomorrow.
ex: that ship has sailed = 時機已過。

line: To be honest, we've had our fingers burned with outsourcing before.
a: That's understandable. What went wrong last time, if you don't mind me asking?
ex: have fingers burned = 吃過虧;先了解過去問題。

line: Let's take this offline.
a: Sure, I'll grab you after the meeting.
d: No, let's discuss it now in front of everyone.
ex: take this offline = 會後私下討論,與網路無關。

line: Could you circle back with legal before we sign off on this?
a: Will do. I'll loop them in today and update you once I hear back.
ex: circle back = 回頭確認;sign off = 正式核准。

ctx: 你趕最後一班車,同事說
line: You're cutting it a bit fine, aren't you?
a: I know — but if the train's on time, I'll make it.
d: I'm cutting it fine, thank you, I like to be fine.
ex: cut it fine = 時間抓得很緊。

line: If you can meet us halfway on price, we can sign today.
a: Halfway is a stretch, but we could do 5% if you extend the contract to two years.
d: Let's meet at the halfway station.
ex: meet halfway = 各退一步;讓步要換取條件。

line: I could be wrong, but isn't the launch date clashing with the trade fair?
a: Good catch — you're right. We should move it.
d: You're wrong. I already checked the calendar and there is no problem.
ex: Good catch = 抓得好;clash = 時間衝突。

line: Your work has been solid, but I'd like to see you take more initiative.
a: That's helpful feedback. Could you give me an example of where I could have stepped up?
ex: 接受回饋並要具體例子;step up = 主動承擔。

line: So, what do you make of all this AI hype?
a: Some of it's justified, but a lot of companies are overpromising.
d: I don't make anything of it, I'm just an engineer, not a businessman.
ex: what do you make of = 你怎麼看;給平衡觀點。

line: Not to nitpick, but the chart's y-axis is mislabelled.
a: Good catch, thanks — fixing it now.
d: Then don't nitpick. Nobody looks at the y-axis anyway.
ex: nitpick = 挑小毛病;大方感謝並修正。

ctx: 朋友猶豫要不要換工作
line: I'm on the fence about whether to take the offer.
a: What's holding you back?
d: Take it, obviously. Are you crazy?
ex: on the fence = 猶豫不決;問顧慮比替人決定好。
